Context
-------
Create a Slidev deck for the 45-minute core session of an observability
workshop. The audience is experienced defence-domain engineers. The deck
is presented live, then attendees move to optional self-paced labs.

Tone: technical, terse, no marketing language. Do not explain what a
metric or a trace is. Assume the audience has run production systems.

This is part of a larger repo that builds an airgapped demo. The deck
lives at slides/ within that repo. It must be usable on a machine with
no network access. All fonts are bundled locally, and no external
requests are made at runtime.

Visual identity
---------------
- Dark, high contrast. Background #0b0d10. Body text #d4d7dc.
  Muted text #7d838c. One accent, used sparingly: amber #ffb454.
- Monospace (JetBrains Mono) for anything that is a name, a number, a
  command, a label, or a code token. Sans (Inter) for prose.
- No images, no icons, no illustrations, no decorative shapes, no logos.
  Text, tables and code only. This is a deliberate constraint — the deck
  should look like documentation, not a pitch.
- CRITICAL: no external font or asset fetches. Bundle fonts locally using
  @fontsource packages. The deck must render fully with the network
  interface down. This will be verified.

Project layout
--------------
slides/
├── package.json
├── slides.md
├── components/BeatCounter.vue
├── layouts/DemoLayout.vue
├── style.css
├── vite.config.ts          # sets base: './' for file:// opening
└── README.md

The slides/ directory is self-contained. It does not share dependencies
with the parent repo. Node modules are not committed. The built static
site and the PDF export are committed under slides/dist/ and
slides/export.pdf respectively.

package.json scripts must include:
  "dev": "slidev",
  "build": "slidev build --base ./",
  "export": "slidev export --output export.pdf"

Headmatter for slides.md:
  theme: default
  title: Introduction to Observability
  author: <leave a clear placeholder>
  highlighter: shiki
  lineNumbers: false
  colorSchema: dark
  fonts:
    sans: Inter
    mono: JetBrains Mono

Main slides — exactly these six, in order
-----------------------------------------

SLIDE 1 — layout: cover
  Title: Introduction to Observability
  Subtitle: a single muted row of the five workshop track names
  separated by middle dots:
    OpenTelemetry · OpenTelemetry for Java · Prometheus ·
    Fluent Bit · Perses
  Speaker notes (~15s): housekeeping. "We demo for 40 minutes, then the
  room opens up and you pick a track. Nothing you're about to see is
  reaching the internet."

SLIDE 2 — layout: statement
  Headline: "In a disconnected environment, you cannot call support.
  You can only know."
  Sub-line, muted, smaller: "Monitoring covers the failures you
  predicted. Observability covers the ones you didn't."
  Speaker notes (~60s): the operative distinction is not tooling, it is
  whether you can ask a question you did not anticipate. That requires
  high-cardinality data, no pre-aggregation, and signals that are
  causally linked. Four tools that don't talk to each other is four
  monitoring tools.

SLIDE 3 — layout: default
  Title: The signals
  A four-row table, two columns, no header row:
    Metrics  | Is something wrong, and how much?
    Traces   | Where in the request path?
    Logs     | What exactly happened?
    Profiles | Which line of code is burning CPU?
  Signal names in mono, accent-coloured. Questions in body text.
  Speaker notes (~60s): they answer different questions; the value is
  moving between them in one click. Metrics are cheap and always-on but
  cardinality-blind. Traces pinpoint but cost. Logs are ground truth
  nobody wants to grep. Mention exemplars link metrics to traces and
  that the OTel-for-Java workshop covers it, then move on — do not let
  this become a taxonomy debate.

SLIDE 4 — layout: default
  Title: What's actually new
  Three numbered items. Number in accent mono. Bold lead-in, then one
  muted line of elaboration:
    1. Telemetry from the kernel.
       eBPF means the CNI sees L7 — status, latency, DNS, flow verdicts —
       with no client library, no sidecar, and no way for the application
       to alter the record.
    2. Policy as code, verified continuously.
       Cilium enforces segmentation; Hubble shows the verdicts. Declare
       the boundary, then prove it holds, every flow, every second.
    3. OTLP as the sovereign interface.
       Instrument once, route to backends you control, over transports
       you control. Nothing has to phone home.
  Speaker notes (~120s): this slide justifies the demo. Land each point
  deliberately and pause after each. On 1: "for fifteen years network
  visibility meant a proxy; now it's the kernel." On 2: "the control and
  the evidence are the same system." On 3: "you are not choosing between
  Fluent Bit and the OTel Collector — Fluent Bit speaks OTLP."

SLIDE 5 — layout: default
  Title: Why this stack
  Two-column table with a header row:
    Criterion        | Position
    Licence          | Apache-2.0 across every component
    Source           | Available. Auditable. Forkable.
    Transport        | Nothing requires a hosted endpoint
    Data residency   | Everything in-boundary
    Longevity        | CNCF projects, not a single-vendor bet
  Criterion column in accent mono.
  Speaker notes (~60s): "You could build this on a commercial platform.
  This is what it looks like when you don't want to."

SLIDE 6 — layout: section
  Text: "Let's break something."
  Speaker notes (~15s): "Everything from here is live. One app, three
  services, and we're going to make it fail in three different ways.
  Watch where each failure shows up first."

Demo interstitials — exactly three
----------------------------------
These are shown during the live demo. Use layout: demo (see below).
Each takes a `beat` frontmatter value so the BeatCounter highlights the
right step.

  SLIDE 7  — layout: demo, beat: 1  — title: Metrics
  SLIDE 8  — layout: demo, beat: 4  — title: Network
  SLIDE 9  — layout: demo, beat: 5  — title: Traces

Each has speaker notes of one sentence naming what the audience is about
to see. Keep these slides visually near-empty: title, and the counter.

Backup slides
-------------
After a `layout: end` slide that reads "Questions", add these. They are
for Q&A only, not for the main run.

B1 — Component versions and licences. Table: component, version, licence,
     one-line role. Populate with placeholders and a comment telling the
     presenter to fill from the parent repo's versions.lock.
B2 — The DemoHighErrorRate PromQL, in a code block, with three one-line
     annotations below explaining the numerator, the denominator, and the
     `for` duration.
B3 — The api-deny-dns CiliumNetworkPolicy YAML in a code block, with two
     lines below: what it denies, and what Hubble shows as a result.
B4 — Links. o11y-workshops.gitlab.io, and the five workshop URLs under
     it, each on its own line.
B5 — How the demo was built: K3S, Cilium with kube-proxy replaced, Helm,
     airgapped, build node and replay node.

Components
----------

components/BeatCounter.vue
  Props: current (Number, required)
  Renders a single horizontal row of 9 beats:
    0 Baseline · 1 Latency · 2 Errors · 3 Alert lifecycle · 4 DNS ·
    5 Traces · 6 Logs · 7 Perses · 8 Recovery
  Styling:
    - 11px JetBrains Mono, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.05em
    - the current beat: accent colour, and a small filled square before it
    - all others: muted text at 55% opacity
    - a thin muted connector line between items
    - the whole row fits within 1200px at 1920x1080
  Must be pure presentational. No state, no listeners.

layouts/DemoLayout.vue
  A layout that renders the slide title large and left-aligned, a lot of
  empty space, and the BeatCounter in the bottom-left footer.
  Reads `beat` from useSlideContext / frontmatter and passes it as
  :current to BeatCounter. If `beat` is absent, do not render the counter.

Do NOT put a BeatCounter on slides 1-6. It is only for the three
interstitials.

style.css
  - import the two @fontsource families
  - set the Slidev CSS variables for background, text and accent
  - table styling: no outer borders, header row in accent mono uppercase
    with a single bottom border, generous row padding, body cells in
    muted-to-body text
  - code block styling: no shadows, subtle border, background one step
    lighter than the page
  - a `statement` layout override making the headline large and centred

vite.config.ts
--------------
Set `base: './'` (or configure it in a slidev config file) so that the
built `dist/` site works when opened directly from the filesystem using
`file://`. This is the key configuration that makes the deck work on an
airgapped machine without a web server.

Static artifact — mandatory
---------------------------
There are two offline artifacts:

1. `slides/dist/` — the static site, produced by `npm run build`.
   It must work when `dist/index.html` is double-clicked and opened via
   `file://`. No absolute paths, no external URLs, no font fetches.
   All assets are relative to the page.

2. `slides/export.pdf` — produced by `npm run export`.
   This is the fallback that opens anywhere. Must be present and contain
   all 16 slides.

Both outputs are committed to the repo. They are generated on a
machine with internet access, then carried to the offline venue.

Speaker notes
-------------
Every slide gets notes in an HTML comment at the end of the slide block.
Write them as spoken prose, not fragments. Expand the summaries above
into complete sentences in the presenter's voice. Notes should be
readable aloud without editing on the day.

README.md (inside slides/)
--------------------------
  - npm install, npm run dev
  - npm run build and npm run export, both requiring network only at
    build time. The built artifacts are committed and carry no runtime
    network dependency.
  - How to verify offline: after building, open `dist/index.html` via
    `file://`, open devtools, confirm the Network tab shows zero requests
    to non-localhost origins. Also confirm `export.pdf` opens correctly.

Constraints
-----------
1. Do not add slides beyond those listed. Nine main, one end, five
   backup. Sixteen total.
2. Do not add images or external URLs in any tag.
3. Prefer tables over bullet lists throughout.
4. The deck must fit a 1920x1080 projector with no text overflow. Slide 5
   is the longest table — check it specifically.
5. Everything must render with the network interface down, in both the
   static site opened via `file://` and the PDF.

Acceptance
----------
1. `npm run dev` serves with no console errors.
2. `npm run build` completes; `dist/index.html` exists. Open it via
   `file://` in a browser. Zero requests to any non-localhost origin,
   confirmed in devtools.
3. `npm run export` completes; `export.pdf` exists and has all 16 pages.
4. The three demo interstitials render the BeatCounter with the correct
   beat highlighted (1, 4, 5 respectively).
5. No main slide overflows at 1920x1080.
Report the result of checks 2, 3, and 4.
